activities.anchor: Control is a numbers game in two dimensions
activities.caption: call the motor unit — precision versus power
activities.name: mtUnitEstimate

config.prompt: One alpha motor neuron plus all the fibres it innervates is a motor unit. Roughly how many fibres are in a unit of the gastrocnemius (calf) muscle?
config.why: About 1,000–2,000 — power over precision. The extraocular muscles that aim the eyes run units of roughly a dozen fibres each, the fine gradation eye movements need.
config.context: Recruitment and rate coding are the two dimensions of the numbers game.

activities.anchor: the two embedded sensors answer different questions
activities.caption: pair each sensor with what it reports
activities.name: mtSensorMatch

config.prompt: Muscle is a sensor organ. Pair each component with its report:

pairs.right: muscle length and, above all, the velocity of stretch via fast Ia afferents
tension — the force the muscle is producing
keeps the spindle taut during contraction so it stays sensitive at every length
shortening a muscle would silence its own sensor

config.why: One measures position and speed, the other load — two questions, two sensors embedded in the same muscle.

activities.anchor: the famous patient I.W. had to relearn movement visually
activities.caption: true or false — muscles as actuators
activities.name: mtUpwardJudge

statements.s: Muscles are dumb actuators that merely receive commands.
statements.why: About a third of the nervous system's traffic with muscle is upward — a continuous report of limb position, speed and load.

statements.s: Spindle and tendon afferents give the spinal cord and cortex a continuous report.
statements.why: Position, speed and load stream upward while commands stream down.

statements.s: Without that upward report, people can still coordinate a reach with their eyes closed.
statements.why: Deprived of it, people cannot coordinate a reach without watching their hands — controlling each joint by eye.

statements.s: Large-fibre sensory neuropathy removes the upward report.
statements.why: It does exactly this — which is how the report's necessity was demonstrated.

activities.anchor: Evolution's solution: hard-wire the most urgent corrections into the cord
activities.caption: rebuild the knee-jerk — the 50-millisecond loop
activities.name: mtReflexOrder

config.prompt: The patellar reflex, from tap to kick. Rebuild the loop:
items: A tap on the tendon stretches the quadriceps
Ia afferents race to the spinal cord at up to 80–120 metres per second
A single synapse excites the alpha motor neurons of the same muscle
The quadriceps contracts — total loop time about 50 milliseconds
config.why: Conscious perception of the tap alone would take around 200 milliseconds of cortical processing — a reflex that consulted the cortex would arrive long after the knee buckled.

activities.anchor: why clinicians use reflex testing as a probe
activities.caption: find the faulty line — reflex-testing notes
activities.name: mtGainSpot

config.prompt: A student's notes on spinal reflexes contain one faulty line — click it:
lines: Descending pathways continuously re-scale reflex gain.
The same tap feels different when you are relaxed, braced or startled.
Reflex gain is fixed at birth and cannot be re-scaled from above.
Reciprocal inhibition suppresses the antagonist during every voluntary action.
config.correction: Reflexes are modulated, not fixed: descending pathways re-scale their gain — hyperreflexia sits above a spinal lesion, absent reflexes at it.
config.why: Reflex circuits also do housekeeping for voluntary movement — muscular bookkeeping offloaded from the cortex.

activities.caption: file each tract — cortex or brainstem
activities.name: mtTractBuckets

config.prompt: Which commands descend from cortex, and which from the brainstem? File each tract:

items.label: roughly a million axons through the internal capsule, crossing at the medullary pyramids
controls distal limb muscles after about 85% decussate

config.why: The crossing explains the bedside facts: a left-hemisphere stroke paralyses the right side, and the level of a spinal injury predicts the loss — C4 takes all four limbs, T6 spares the arms.

activities.anchor: The timing experiments are the strangest result in the field
activities.caption: place the marker — when awareness arrived
activities.name: mtLibetPlace

config.prompt: Kornhuber and Deecke found cortical preparation beginning up to a second or more before a self-timed finger movement. Place the marker at when Libet's subjects reported becoming aware of their decision:
config.why: About 200 milliseconds before moving — long after the brain began preparing the action. Libet himself proposed a final veto; the naive picture of a self issuing commands into a passive body did not survive.

activities.anchor: The cerebellum is about 10% of brain volume
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the forward model
activities.name: mtCerebellumCloze

config.text: In computational terms the cerebellum runs a %%0%% model: it predicts the %%1%% consequence of the command and flags the mismatch. Climbing fibres carry the %%2%% signal, and long-term %%3%% at the parallel-fibre-Purkinje synapse slowly retunes the prediction.
config.hint: The first blank names the kind of model; the last is the synaptic change doing the retuning.
